title: Tulane Band and learning by sitting in with New Orleans bands
summary: He took up music again at 18 with the Tulane Band, then sat in with other bands on violin, learning by playing, until hired regularly.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the horn: first instrument and the trombone

blocks.x: Was that a dance band or a brass band?

Yes, a regular orchestra. It started with him. I stayed with him until I got better, and I moved from there and went further around town in New Orleans, you know, another neighborhood. Got acquainted with a lot of the upper musicians. Going with one band this night, another one, playing in with the band, taking my violin with me, and playing in with the other fellas, you see. That's what brought me on through with my music. Just might as well say I stole it. You know how they... That was wonderful. And by some fellas, I could make out with the band by practicing with them like that, you know, and when they wanted to lay off, they'd give me a night to work. And they'd continue like that for three or four times a week. They'd follow different bands. Every band you play with, playing violin, you were a leader at that time. You had to lead the band. So I worked up myself good enough to be hired from different bands until I got in regular band. And when I started playing, that was 1910, I started in the Red Lake District. That was Frankie Haney on piano, Manuel Perez playing cornet. I was playing violin. Which place did you work? That was Mr. Tom Anderson's room.
